terms.grammar: adverb; “rather than” is potius quam, with the subjunctive when two actions are compared
evidence: Cic. Tusc. 2.52: perpessus est omnia potius quam cōnsciōs indicāret (Lewis & Short)

terms.grammar: verb, irregular, with an infinitive; “rather than” is quam
evidence: Quint. 1.1.12: ā sermōne Graecō puerum incipere mālō
terms.comment: “I’d rather” is the verb itself: mālō; politely, mālim.

evidence: Quint. 12.10.29: paene nōn hūmānā vōce vel omnīnō nōn vōce potius
Cic. Brut. 332: propemodum, vel plānē potius (Lewis & Short)

terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to place before another in esteem, to prefer” (very frequent).

terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation: aliquid alicui antepōnere
evidence: Cic. Amic. 17: amīcitiam omnibus rēbus hūmānīs antepōnātis

phrases.english: I’d rather hear it from you in person

phrases.latin: Hoc patrium est, potius cōnsuēfacere fīlium suā sponte rēctē facere quam aliēnō metū.
phrases.english: That is a father’s part: to get a son used to doing right of his own accord, rather than from fear of someone else.

phrases.latin: vel sōlī tamen dīcāmus potius quam omnīnō nōn dīcāmus
phrases.english: let us speak even on our own, rather than not speak at all

phrases.latin: ego vōs hortārī tantum possum, ut amīcitiam omnibus rēbus hūmānīs antepōnātis
phrases.english: all I can do is urge you to put friendship before everything else in human life
